hints.title: Independent Digit Choices
hints.text: Even digits (0, 2, 4, 6, 8) offer 5 independent choices; prime digits (2, 3, 5, 7) offer 4 independent choices.

hints.title: Index Parity Partitions
hints.text: in a string of length n, there are (n + 1) // 2 even indices and n // 2 odd indices.

hints.title: Modular Exponentiation
hints.text: compute (5^even_count * 4^odd_count) modulo 10^9 + 7 using fast modular exponentiation.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def countGoodNumbers(self, n: int) -> int:
        MOD = 10**9 + 7
        even_count = (n + 1) // 2
        odd_count = n // 2
        return (pow(5, even_count, MOD) * pow(4, odd_count, MOD)) % MOD
```

complexity.notes: Binary modular exponentiation computes powers of 5 and 4 modulo 10^9 + 7.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Iterative multiplication takes O(N) operations, which times out for N up to 10^15.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Fast binary modular exponentiation runs in O(log N) time with O(1) space.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should recognize independent product rule and binary exponentiation.
